newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia-IMF talks will not be easy - econ minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia-IMF talks will not be easy - econ minister.

text.p: Russia's talks with the International Monetary Fund on the next tranche of a $10 billion loan will not be easy because of shortfalls in tax collection, Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin said on Wednesday.
"I do not think the discussion with them will be easy," he told a news conference.
An IMF mission arrived in Moscow on Wednesday and discussions are due to begin on Thursday.
Yasin said a main talking point would be poor tax revenues, which totalled a low 2.2 trillion roubles in cash in the first nine days of October.
Overall tax receipts are about 40 percent below targeted levels.
The IMF had delayed payment of one of its summer tranches over tax shortfall worries, but later released the $300 million tranche.
President Boris Yeltsin set up an emergency commission last week, headed by Prime Minister Victor Chernomyrdin, to improve tax collection.
The government has threatened six big companies with bankruptcy if they fail to pay tax arrears within a week.
But Yasin said Russia had fulfilled the IMF's main demand -- that of not increasing the budget deficit.
"As regards our key committments, we have been meeting them against all odds," he said.
"Shortfalls in tax collection are not being compensated by printing money or by heavier borrowing on the markets. Therefore, the budget deficit is not growing -- and this is very difficult."
